1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 Axel Delaval. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	-/
     5	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivDegree
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SchematicSupport
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RigidPushforwardTransfer
     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FlatteningStratificationUniversal
     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# Pushing a divisor family down to the base, flatly
    12	
    13	Campaign milestone **D3'** (`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md:305`) asks
    14	for the locus over which a Grassmannian `T`-point arises from a degree-`d`
    15	`DivFamily` to be locally closed *universally*, by extending
    16	`AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal`
    17	(`Picard/FlatteningStratificationUniversal.lean`) "to the family `C × G → G`".
    18	
    19	This file supplies the object that extension has to be about, and records why the
    20	extension has to be phrased this way rather than by relativising the machine.
    21	
    22	## The shape of the reduction, and why it is forced
    23	
    24	`flatLocusStratification_universal` is stated for a module **on the base**,
    25	`F : S.Modules`, with `π = 𝟙 S`. That is not an accident of its proof that a
    26	later session can relax: the whole stratification machine is built on
    27	`Scheme.Modules.pointRank : (X : Scheme) → X.Modules → ↥X → ℕ`, which takes a
    28	module on *one* scheme and a point of *that* scheme. There is no relative
    29	`pointRank` over a morphism, and `chartLocus`, `rankStratum`,
    30	`isOpen_pointRank_pullback_eq` and `existsUnique_factor_rankStratum` all inherit
    31	that shape. So a general-`π` universal property cannot be obtained by adding a
    32	`π` to those statements; the family has to be *moved to the base* first.
    33	
    34	For a divisor family that move is available, and cheaply, because a relative
    35	effective divisor is finite over the base — where a general proper family is not.
    36	Concretely: `Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport` is by definition
    37	`IsProper (schematicSupportι F ≫ f)` (`Picard/QuotScheme.lean`), and
    38	`DivFamily.properSupport` is exactly that datum for `f = pullback.snd π T.hom`.
    39	A proper *quasi-finite* morphism is finite (`IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite`),
    40	hence affine, and `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat` transfers along an affine
    41	pushforward. Since `O_D` is the pushforward of its own restriction to the support
    42	(`schematicSupportDescentIso`), the family's flatness over `T` becomes flatness of
    43	`q_* O_D` over `T` *itself* — the `n = 0` shape the universal property consumes.
    44	
    45	## What is proved here, and what is assumed
    46	
    47	* `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.of_pushforward_of_isAffineHom` — the **converse** of
    48	  `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom`
    49	  (`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`), which did not exist. Both directions
    50	  are the same chart computation read in opposite directions; the content is that
    51	  the two `Γ(T, U)`-module structures on `Γ(F, π ⁻¹ᵁ V)` agree, which is
    52	  `Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE`.
    53	
    54	* `Scheme.DivFamily.coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward` — for a divisor family whose
    55	  divisor is quasi-finite over the base, `q_* O_D` is flat over `T` in the
    56	  `CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T.left)` sense.
    57	
    58	**The quasi-finiteness is a hypothesis, not a theorem, and this file does not
    59	pretend otherwise.** `LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)`
    60	says the divisor `D ⊆ X_T` has finite fibres over `T`. Mathematically it is
    61	relative-dimension-1 content: on the curve fibre `C_t`, `D_t` is the zero scheme
    62	of a regular section of an invertible ideal, hence `0`-dimensional. It has no
    63	producer in this project, and `LocallyQuasiFinite` occurs nowhere else in
    64	`Picard/`. It is stated as an instance binder so that a later producer discharges
    65	every consumer at once.
    66	
    67	Worth recording for whoever prices the next step: this hypothesis is *cleaner*
    68	than the one it replaces. `Picard/DivDegree.lean` gates its clopen degree
    69	decomposition on `HasLocallyConstantDivDeg`, a `Prop`-class carrying local
    70	constancy of `fiberDeg` as an assumption and also without a producer. With
    71	quasi-finiteness instead, local constancy is downstream of a stratification
    72	theorem rather than assumed beside it — the same missing geometry, but bought
    73	once and in a form the machine can use.
    74	
    75	## What remains for D3'
    76	
    77	`flatLocusStratification_universal` has exactly **two** binders:
    78	`[IsNoetherian S]` and `[F.IsFinitePresentation]`. `IsQuasicoherent` is a mathlib
    79	instance *from* finite presentation, so it is not a separate requirement;
    80	`DivFamily.isQuasicoherent_pushforward` below is kept because it is the cheap half

    89	  `IsFinite.finite_app` — this is where the finiteness of the support map is spent,

   134	/-- **Coherent-sheaf flatness descends along an affine pushforward** — the
   135	converse of `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom`.
   136	
   137	For affine `π : X ⟶ Y` over `p : Y ⟶ T`, flatness of `π_* F` over `T` gives
   138	flatness of `F` over `T` along the composite. Read on an affine `V ⊆ Y`: the
   139	sections of `π_* F` over `V` *are* `Γ(F, π ⁻¹ᵁ V)` definitionally, with `π ⁻¹ᵁ V`
   140	affine because `π` is, and the two `Γ(T, U)`-module structures agree because
   141	`(π ≫ p).appLE = p.appLE ≫ π.appLE`.
   142	
   143	Flatness on the preimage charts `π ⁻¹ᵁ V` of an affine cover of `Y` is what the
   144	hypothesis gives directly; `flat_section_of_affine_cover` globalises it to every
   145	affine pair of `X`, which is where quasi-coherence of `F` is used. -/
   146	theorem Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.of_pushforward_of_isAffineHom
   147	    {X Y T : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom π] (p : Y ⟶ T)
   148	    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
   149	    (h : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat p ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward π).obj F)) :
   150	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (π ≫ p) F := by
   151	  classical
   152	  -- For each point of `X` pick an affine `V ⊆ Y` around its image together with an
   153	  -- affine `U ⊆ T` above it; `π ⁻¹ᵁ V` is then affine because `π` is.
   154	  have hchart : ∀ x : X, ∃ (V : Y.Opens) (U : T.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V)
   155	      (_ : IsAffineOpen U), π.base x ∈ V ∧ V ≤ p ⁻¹ᵁ U := by
   156	    intro x
   157	    obtain ⟨U, hUaff, hU, -⟩ :=
   158	      exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset (x := p.base (π.base x)) (U := ⊤) trivial
   159	    obtain ⟨V, hVaff, hxV, hVU⟩ :=
   160	      exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset (x := π.base x) (U := p ⁻¹ᵁ U) hU
   161	    exact ⟨V, U, hVaff, hUaff, hxV, hVU⟩
   162	  choose Vc Uc hVc hUc hmem hle using hchart
   163	  intro U₀ hU₀ V₀ hV₀ e₀
   164	  refine flat_section_of_affine_cover (π ≫ p) F
   165	    (fun x => π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x) (fun x => (hVc x).preimage π)
   166	    Uc hUc (fun x => ?_) (fun x => ⟨x, hmem x⟩) (fun x => ?_) hU₀ hV₀ e₀
   167	  · -- `π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x ≤ (π ≫ p) ⁻¹ᵁ Uc x`
   168	    rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage]
   169	    exact fun z hz => hle x hz
   170	  · -- the chart flatness, read off the hypothesis at `Vc x`
   171	    have base := h (hUc x) (hVc x) (hle x)
   172	    have hφ : ((π ≫ p).appLE (Uc x) (π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x)
   173	          (by rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage]; exact fun z hz => hle x hz)).hom =
   174	        ((π.app (Vc x)).hom).comp ((p.appLE (Uc x) (Vc x) (hle x)).hom) := by
   175	      have h1 := Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE π p (Uc x) (Vc x) (π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x)
   176	        (hle x) le_rfl
   177	      refine RingHom.ext fun r => ?_
   178	      have h2 := congrArg
   179	        (fun (φ : Γ(T, Uc x) ⟶ Γ(X, π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x)) => φ.hom r) h1
   180	      simp only [CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.comp_apply] at h2
   181	      rw [RingHom.comp_apply, Scheme.Hom.app_eq_appLE]
   182	      exact h2.symm
   183	    change @Module.Flat _ _ _ _ (Module.compHom Γ(F, π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x)
   184	      ((π ≫ p).appLE (Uc x) (π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x) _).hom)
   185	    rw [hφ]
   186	    exact base

   188	/-- **The pushforward of `O_D` is flat over the base itself.**
   189	
   190	For a divisor family `x` whose divisor is quasi-finite over `T`, the pushforward
   191	`q_* O_D` along `q = pullback.snd π T.hom` is flat over `T` in the
   192	`CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T.left)` sense.
   193	
   194	This is the `n = 0` shape, but **not literally what
   195	`AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal` asks for**: its antecedent
   196	carries a pullback along the test morphism, which at `φ = 𝟙` is not reduced away.
   197	The bridged form is `coherentSheafFlat_id_pullbackId_pushforward` below.
   198	
   199	Route: `x.properSupport` is `IsProper (i ≫ q)` by definition, so with
   200	quasi-finiteness `i ≫ q` is finite, hence affine; `schematicSupportDescentIso`
   201	presents `x.F` as `i_*` of its restriction to the support, whose flatness over
   202	`T` follows from `x.flat` by the converse above; pushing forward along the affine
   203	`i ≫ q` over `𝟙 T.left` and transporting along `pushforwardComp` gives the
   204	claim. -/
   205	theorem Scheme.DivFamily.coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward
   206	    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S} (x : Scheme.DivFamily π T)
   207	    [LocallyQuasiFinite
   208	      (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)] :
   209	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
   210	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F) := by
   211	  letI := x.isFinitePresentation
   212	  haveI : x.F.IsQuasicoherent := inferInstance
   213	  set q := pullback.snd π T.hom with hq
   214	  set i := Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F with hi
   215	  -- `i ≫ q` is proper by the divisor family's own support datum, hence finite,
   216	  -- hence affine.
   217	  haveI : IsProper (i ≫ q) := x.properSupport
   218	  haveI : IsFinite (i ≫ q) := IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite _
   219	  haveI : IsAffineHom (i ≫ q) := inferInstance
   220	  haveI : IsAffineHom i :=
   221	    inferInstanceAs (IsAffineHom (Scheme.Modules.annihilator x.F).subschemeι)
   222	  -- present `O_D` as `i_*` of its restriction to the support
   223	  set N := (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj x.F with hN
   224	  have hdesc : x.F ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj N :=
   225	    Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportDescentIso x.F
   226	  haveI : N.IsQuasicoherent := pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom i x.F inferInstance
   227	  -- flatness of `i_* N` over `T`, transported from the family's flatness
   228	  have h1 : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat q ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj N) :=
   229	    coherentSheafFlat_of_iso q hdesc x.flat
   230	  -- descend it to `N` along the affine `i`
   231	  have h2 : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (i ≫ q) N :=
   232	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.of_pushforward_of_isAffineHom i q N h1
   233	  -- push forward along the affine `i ≫ q`, over the identity of the base
   234	  have h3 : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
   235	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (i ≫ q)).obj N) :=
   236	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom (i ≫ q)
   237	      (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u})) N (by rwa [Category.comp_id])
   238	  -- and identify `(i ≫ q)_* N ≅ q_* (i_* N) ≅ q_* O_D`
   239	  intro U hU V hV eV
   240	  exact coherentSheafFlat_of_iso (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
   241	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforwardComp i q).app N ≪≫
   242	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).mapIso hdesc.symm) h3 hU hV eV
   243	
   244	/-- **`q_* O_D` is quasi-coherent** when the ambient family is proper.
   245	
   246	Free: properness of `π` gives `QuasiCompact` and `QuasiSeparated` of the projection
   247	`q = pullback.snd π T.hom` by base change, and pushforward along a qcqs morphism
   248	preserves quasi-coherence.
   249	
   250	Not a binder of `AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal`, which asks
   251	only for `[IsNoetherian S]` and `[F.IsFinitePresentation]` — quasi-coherence is a
   252	mathlib instance from the latter. Kept because it is wanted in its own right and is
   253	the cheap half of the pair. -/
   254	theorem Scheme.DivFamily.isQuasicoherent_pushforward
   255	    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} [IsProper π] {T : Over S}
   256	    (x : Scheme.DivFamily π T) :
   257	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F).IsQuasicoherent := by
   258	  letI := x.isFinitePresentation
   259	  exact Scheme.Modules.pushforward_isQuasicoherent _ x.F
   260	
   261	/-- **The `φ = 𝟙` instance of `flatLocusStratification_universal`'s antecedent.**
   262	
   263	`:876` asks, for a test morphism `φ : T' ⟶ S`, for
   264	`CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T') ((Modules.pullback φ).obj F)`. At `φ = 𝟙` that is *not*
   265	literally `coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward`: the identity pullback is not reduced
   266	away, so the carrier is `Γ((pullback (𝟙 T.left)).obj (q_* O_D), V)` where the
   267	theorem above supplies `Γ(q_* O_D, V)`. This states the bridged form, so that
   268	consumers do not have to rediscover which of the two shapes they hold.
   269	
   270	Note what this does and does not give: the `φ = 𝟙` **instance** of the antecedent,
   271	not the antecedent as a family over all `φ`. -/
   272	theorem Scheme.DivFamily.coherentSheafFlat_id_pullbackId_pushforward
   273	    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S} (x : Scheme.DivFamily π T)
   274	    [LocallyQuasiFinite
   275	      (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)] :
   276	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
   277	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))).obj
   278	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F)) := by
   279	  intro U hU V hV eV
   280	  exact coherentSheafFlat_of_iso (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))

    15	This file states and attacks the representability of the relative Grassmannian
    16	functor `Grass(V, d) : (Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type 1` (`Scheme.Grassmannian`,
    17	`QuotFunctorDef.lean`) by an `S`-scheme, for `V` a locally free
    18	`O_S`-module of rank `r` and `1 ≤ d ≤ r` ([Nitsure] §1, Exercise (2);
    19	blueprint `thm:grassmannian_representable`).
    20	
    21	The statement here **corrects** the earlier skeleton of `QuotFunctorDef.lean`,
    22	which quantified over an arbitrary sheaf of modules `V` with no rank data:
    23	that form is not the [Nitsure] theorem (whose hypotheses are `V` locally free
    24	of rank `r ≥ d ≥ 1`) and is not known to be true for non-quasi-coherent `V`.
    25	The universe is pinned to `Scheme.{0}`: the merged absolute chart construction
    26	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.scheme` / `.represents`,
    27	`GrassmannianQuot.lean`) lives over the genuinely terminal `Spec ℤ` of
    28	`Scheme.{0}`, and the relative theorem is obtained from it.
    29	
    30	## Contents
    31	
    32	* `Scheme.LocallyFreeQuotient.congrModule` / `Scheme.Grassmannian.congrIso` —
    33	  transport of the Grassmannian functor along an isomorphism `V ≅ V'` of the
    34	  classified module (pure functoriality, no pseudofunctor coherence).
    35	* `Scheme.LocallyFreeQuotient.toRankQuotient` / `.ofRankQuotient` /
    36	  `Scheme.Grassmannian.freeCompare` — for the free module `V = O_S^r`, the
    37	  comparison `Grass(O_S^r, d) ≅ (Over.forget S)ᵒᵖ ⋙ Grass(r, d)` with the
    38	  merged absolute Grassmannian functor, re-presenting the pulled-back free
    39	  module through `Scheme.Modules.pullbackFreeIso`.  Naturality is the free
    40	  coherence `pullbackFreeIso_comp` of `GlueDescent.lean`.
    41	* `Scheme.Grassmannian.prodRepresentableBy` — the absolute Grassmannian,
    42	  pulled back to `Over S` along the forgetful functor, is representable by
    43	  the product `S ⨯ Gr(d, r)` with its first projection (`Spec ℤ` is terminal
    44	  in `Scheme.{0}`, so the product is the base change of `Gr(d, r)` to `S`).
    45	* `Scheme.Grassmannian.representable_of_iso_free` — representability of
    46	  `Grass(V, d)` for globally trivialised `V ≅ O_S^r` (complete proof).
    47	* `Scheme.Grassmannian.representable` — the [Nitsure] statement, for `V`
    48	  locally free of rank `r`: glue `representable_of_iso_free` over a
    49	  trivialising cover of `(S, V)` by Zariski descent of representability
    50	  (`Scheme.representable_of_openCover`, proved in
    51	  `ZariskiDescentRepresentability.lean`); the remaining leaf is the sheaf
    52	  axiom `Grassmannian.isZariskiSheaf`.
    53

    57	(`blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`).

    20	change — to the *sheaf* statement that `p_* M` is locally free of rank
    21	`p.fiberH0 M t` near every `t : Spec A`.

    23	This file supplies the **sheaf** half of that upgrade, i.e. everything except
    24	the rank identification:

    27	  localisation morphism `Spec R_f ⟶ Spec R` is the basic open `D(f)`.
    28	* `Module.free_and_finrank_of_isLocalizedModule` — freeness and rank pass

    38	  crux: a quasi-coherent module on `Spec R` whose global sections are finite

    76	immersion `D(f) ↪ Spec R`, so its set-theoretic range is the range of that
    77	immersion, namely `D(f)` itself (`Scheme.Opens.range_ι`). -/

    10	/-!
    11	# Pushing a divisor family down to the base, flatly
    12	
    13	Campaign milestone **D3'** (`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md:305`) asks
    14	for the locus over which a Grassmannian `T`-point arises from a degree-`d`
    15	`DivFamily` to be locally closed *universally*, by extending
    16	`AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal`
    17	(`Picard/FlatteningStratificationUniversal.lean`) "to the family `C × G → G`".
    18	
    19	This file supplies the object that extension has to be about, and records why the
    20	extension has to be phrased this way rather than by relativising the machine.
    21	
    22	## The shape of the reduction, and why it is forced
    23	
    24	`flatLocusStratification_universal` is stated for a module **on the base**,
    25	`F : S.Modules`, with `π = 𝟙 S`. That is not an accident of its proof that a
    26	later session can relax: the whole stratification machine is built on
    27	`Scheme.Modules.pointRank : (X : Scheme) → X.Modules → ↥X → ℕ`, which takes a
    28	module on *one* scheme and a point of *that* scheme. There is no relative
    29	`pointRank` over a morphism, and `chartLocus`, `rankStratum`,
    30	`isOpen_pointRank_pullback_eq` and `existsUnique_factor_rankStratum` all inherit
    31	that shape. So a general-`π` universal property cannot be obtained by adding a
    32	`π` to those statements; the family has to be *moved to the base* first.
    33	
    34	For a divisor family that move is available, and cheaply, because a relative
    35	effective divisor is finite over the base — where a general proper family is not.
    36	Concretely: `Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport` is by definition
    37	`IsProper (schematicSupportι F ≫ f)` (`Picard/QuotScheme.lean`), and
    38	`DivFamily.properSupport` is exactly that datum for `f = pullback.snd π T.hom`.
    39	A proper *quasi-finite* morphism is finite (`IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite`),
    40	hence affine, and `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat` transfers along an affine
    41	pushforward. Since `O_D` is the pushforward of its own restriction to the support
    42	(`schematicSupportDescentIso`), the family's flatness over `T` becomes flatness of
    43	`q_* O_D` over `T` *itself* — the `n = 0` shape the universal property consumes.
    44	
    45	## What is proved here, and what is assumed
    46	
    47	* `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.of_pushforward_of_isAffineHom` — the **converse** of
    48	  `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom`
    49	  (`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`), which did not exist. Both directions
    50	  are the same chart computation read in opposite directions; the content is that
    51	  the two `Γ(T, U)`-module structures on `Γ(F, π ⁻¹ᵁ V)` agree, which is
    52	  `Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE`.
    53	
    54	* `Scheme.DivFamily.coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward` — for a divisor family whose
    55	  divisor is quasi-finite over the base, `q_* O_D` is flat over `T` in the
    56	  `CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T.left)` sense.
    57	
    58	**The quasi-finiteness is a hypothesis, not a theorem, and this file does not
    59	pretend otherwise.** `LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)`
    60	says the divisor `D ⊆ X_T` has finite fibres over `T`. Mathematically it is
    61	relative-dimension-1 content: on the curve fibre `C_t`, `D_t` is the zero scheme
    62	of a regular section of an invertible ideal, hence `0`-dimensional. It has no
    63	producer in this project, and `LocallyQuasiFinite` occurs nowhere else in
    64	`Picard/`. It is stated as an instance binder so that a later producer discharges
    65	every consumer at once.
    66	
    67	Worth recording for whoever prices the next step: this hypothesis is *cleaner*
    68	than the one it replaces. `Picard/DivDegree.lean` gates its clopen degree
    69	decomposition on `HasLocallyConstantDivDeg`, a `Prop`-class carrying local
    70	constancy of `fiberDeg` as an assumption and also without a producer. With
    71	quasi-finiteness instead, local constancy is downstream of a stratification
    72	theorem rather than assumed beside it — the same missing geometry, but bought
    73	once and in a form the machine can use.
    74	
    75	## What remains for D3'
    76	
    77	`flatLocusStratification_universal` has exactly **two** binders:
    78	`[IsNoetherian S]` and `[F.IsFinitePresentation]`. `IsQuasicoherent` is a mathlib
    79	instance *from* finite presentation, so it is not a separate requirement;
    80	`DivFamily.isQuasicoherent_pushforward` below is kept because it is the cheap half
    81	and is wanted in its own right, not because `:876` asks for it.
    82	
    83	Finite presentation of `q_* O_D` is `DivFamily.isFinitePresentation_pushforward`,
    84	proved here. `isFinitePresentation_of_finite_sections`
    85	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`) reduces it to `Module.Finite Γ(T,V)
    86	Γ(q_* O_D, V)` on affine `V`, and that tower is:
    87	
    88	* `Module.Finite Γ(T,V) Γ(D,W)` for `W := (i ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V`, from
    89	  `IsFinite.finite_app` — this is where the finiteness of the support map is spent,
    90	  and it is exactly what quasi-finiteness bought;
    91	* `Module.Finite Γ(D,W) Γ(N,W)` from `finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom`
    92	  together with `isFinitePresentation_pullback_schematicSupportι`;
    93	* the two compose by `Module.Finite.trans`, and the result transports back across
    94	  `schematicSupportDescentIso` because `Γ(q_* F, V) = Γ(F, q ⁻¹ᵁ V)` and
    95	  `Γ(i_* N, q ⁻¹ᵁ V) = Γ(N, (i ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V)` are both `rfl`, and the native
    96	  `Γ(T,V)`-action on `Γ(q_* F, V)` *is* `compHom` along `q.app V`, also `rfl`. The
    97	  semilinearity is `Scheme.Modules.Hom.app_smul`.
    98	
    99	## What remains for D3'
   100	
   101	Two things, and neither is supplied here.
   102	
   103	**A stated bridge, not a free fit.** `:876` stratifies a module on the base and
   104	quantifies its universal property over test morphisms `φ : T' ⟶ S`; its antecedent
   105	asks for `CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T') ((Modules.pullback φ).obj F)`. What
   106	`coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward` gives is the `φ = 𝟙` case *before* the identity
   107	pullback is reduced, so feeding it needs
   108	`(Scheme.Modules.pullbackId T.left).app _` through `coherentSheafFlat_of_iso` —
   109	one line, but a line, and it discharges the `φ = 𝟙` **instance** rather than the
   110	antecedent as a family. Whether that instance is what D3' needs is not settled in
   111	this file and should be settled before D3' is priced as "inputs done".
   112	
   113	**The `∃!` statement about the Grassmannian locus itself**, which is D3' proper.
   114	
   115	Nothing in this file closes D3'.
   116	
   117	## Honest status of every antecedent
   118	
   119	`Scheme.DivFamily` itself has **no producer anywhere in this project** — 135
   120	mention sites, all consumers (measured 2026-07-29, inbox `I-0957`). So the
   121	theorems here, like the rest of Cluster D', are true statements about a carrier
   122	nobody has yet inhabited; that is a property of the cluster, not of this file, and
   123	it is recorded rather than hidden. The `LocallyQuasiFinite` binder has no producer
   124	either, and is *not* derivable from `DivFamily`'s other fields (kernel-checked),
   125	so it is genuine content and not a restatement of `properSupport`.
   126	-/

   134	/-- **Coherent-sheaf flatness descends along an affine pushforward** — the
   135	converse of `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom`.
   136	
   137	For affine `π : X ⟶ Y` over `p : Y ⟶ T`, flatness of `π_* F` over `T` gives
   138	flatness of `F` over `T` along the composite. Read on an affine `V ⊆ Y`: the
   139	sections of `π_* F` over `V` *are* `Γ(F, π ⁻¹ᵁ V)` definitionally, with `π ⁻¹ᵁ V`
   140	affine because `π` is, and the two `Γ(T, U)`-module structures agree because
   141	`(π ≫ p).appLE = p.appLE ≫ π.appLE`.
   142	
   143	Flatness on the preimage charts `π ⁻¹ᵁ V` of an affine cover of `Y` is what the
   144	hypothesis gives directly; `flat_section_of_affine_cover` globalises it to every
   145	affine pair of `X`, which is where quasi-coherence of `F` is used. -/

   147	    {X Y T : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom π] (p : Y ⟶ T)
   148	    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
   149	    (h : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat p ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward π).obj F)) :
   150	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (π ≫ p) F := by
   151	  classical
   152	  -- For each point of `X` pick an affine `V ⊆ Y` around its image together with an
   153	  -- affine `U ⊆ T` above it; `π ⁻¹ᵁ V` is then affine because `π` is.
   154	  have hchart : ∀ x : X, ∃ (V : Y.Opens) (U : T.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V)
   155	      (_ : IsAffineOpen U), π.base x ∈ V ∧ V ≤ p ⁻¹ᵁ U := by
   156	    intro x
   157	    obtain ⟨U, hUaff, hU, -⟩ :=
   158	      exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset (x := p.base (π.base x)) (U := ⊤) trivial
   159	    obtain ⟨V, hVaff, hxV, hVU⟩ :=
   160	      exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset (x := π.base x) (U := p ⁻¹ᵁ U) hU
   161	    exact ⟨V, U, hVaff, hUaff, hxV, hVU⟩
   162	  choose Vc Uc hVc hUc hmem hle using hchart
   163	  intro U₀ hU₀ V₀ hV₀ e₀
   164	  refine flat_section_of_affine_cover (π ≫ p) F
   165	    (fun x => π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x) (fun x => (hVc x).preimage π)
   166	    Uc hUc (fun x => ?_) (fun x => ⟨x, hmem x⟩) (fun x => ?_) hU₀ hV₀ e₀
   167	  · -- `π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x ≤ (π ≫ p) ⁻¹ᵁ Uc x`
   168	    rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage]
   169	    exact fun z hz => hle x hz
   170	  · -- the chart flatness, read off the hypothesis at `Vc x`
   171	    have base := h (hUc x) (hVc x) (hle x)
   172	    have hφ : ((π ≫ p).appLE (Uc x) (π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x)
   173	          (by rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage]; exact fun z hz => hle x hz)).hom =
   174	        ((π.app (Vc x)).hom).comp ((p.appLE (Uc x) (Vc x) (hle x)).hom) := by

    12	/-!
    13	# The relative-divisor functor `Div_{X/S}` (real definition)
    14	
    15	This file constructs the relative-effective-divisor functor
    16	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.DivFunctor π : (Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1)` of Kleiman,
    17	"The Picard scheme", §3 (Def. `df:red` + Def. `df:div`; FGA Explained Ch. 9,
    18	arXiv:math/0504020), the source of the Abel map of the A.2.c FGA assembly
    19	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, whose `divFunctor` carrier this file
    20	makes real).
    21	
    22	## Encoding decision (quotient encoding)
    23	
    24	Kleiman §3 Def. `df:red`/`df:div`: a *relative effective divisor* on `X_T/T`
    25	is a closed subscheme `D ⊆ X_T` whose ideal `I` is **invertible** and which is
    26	**`T`-flat**; `Div_{X/S}(T)` is the set of such `D`.  We encode a divisor by
    27	its structure-sheaf quotient — the same encoding by which `Div ⊆ Hilb =
    28	Quot_{O}` sits inside the Quot functor (Kleiman §3 Thm. `th:repDiv`): a
    29	`DivFamily π T` is a `Scheme.QuotFamily`-shaped structure with `E` the unit
    30	module `O_X` (so `q : O_{X_T} ⟶ F` up to the canonical isomorphism
    31	`(pr₁)^* O_X ≅ O_{X_T}`; we state the source of `q` verbatim as the pullback
    32	of the unit, exactly as `QuotFamily` does for a general `E`, so that the whole
    33	pullback/functoriality skeleton of `QuotFunctorDef.lean` is reusable), and the
    34	**divisor condition** is: the kernel ideal `I = ker q` is invertible, encoded
    35	by the project-side line-bundle predicate
    36	`Scheme.LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial (kernel q)` (locally trivial of rank one,
    37	Stacks 01HK — the same predicate that carves the line bundles out of
    38	`Scheme.Modules` in `Picard/LineBundlePullback.lean`).  Between the two
    39	candidate encodings of invertibility (a bundled mono `ι : I ⟶ O` with a
    40	cokernel identification, versus the predicate on the categorical kernel) we
    41	choose the **kernel predicate**: `X.Modules` is abelian, so `ker q` is
    42	available functorially with no extra data fields, the equivalence relation on
    43	families stays literally that of the Quot functor (`ker q = ker q'` — no
    44	well-definedness burden for extra fields), and invertibility-of-an-object is
    45	exactly what `IsLocallyTrivial` and its proved pullback-stability
    46	(`IsLocallyTrivial.pullback`, Stacks 01HH) speak about.
    47	
    48	Two families are equivalent iff an isomorphism of the targets commutes with
    49	the quotient maps — equivalently `ker q = ker q'` as subobjects of `O_{X_T}`,
    50	i.e. the two quotients cut out the same closed subscheme `D`.  The value
    51	`DivFunctor π |_T` is the quotient by this relation, so it is Kleiman's *set*
    52	of relative effective divisors on `X_T/T`, not a groupoid of quotients.
    53	
    54	Faithfulness notes (Kleiman §3):
    55	
    56	* the fields `isFinitePresentation` and `properSupport` do not shrink the set
    57	  of divisors in the intended regime: `F = O_D = coker(I ⟶ O)` with `I`
    58	  invertible is automatically finitely presented, and for the FGA
    59	  instantiation (`π` proper, e.g. the curve `C/k`) the schematic support `D`
    60	  is a closed subscheme of the `T`-proper `X_T`, hence automatically proper
    61	  over `T`.  They are included to keep the family shape identical to
    62	  `QuotFamily` (Div sits inside Hilb) and to reuse its base-change lemmas
    63	  verbatim;
    64	* there is **no Hilbert-polynomial field**: Kleiman's `Div_{X/S}` (`df:div`)
    65	  is not filtered by `Φ` — the degree decomposition `Div = ∐_m Div^m`
    66	  (Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`) is a later, separate refinement;
    67	* no hypotheses on `π` are needed for the *functor* (Kleiman `df:div` imposes
    68	  none; projectivity/flatness enter only in the representability theorem
    69	  `th:repDiv`, which is not stated in this file).
    70	
    71	## Base-change well-definedness
    72	
    73	The pullback action reuses the `QuotFamily` base-change lemmas for the shared
    74	fields (finite presentation: `Modules.pullback_isFinitePresentation`, proved;
    75	flatness: `CoherentSheafFlat.of_isPullback`, proved; proper support:
    76	`Modules.HasProperSupport.of_isPullback`, proved in
    77	`Picard/QuotSupportBaseChange.lean`) and needs exactly one new fact for the
    78	divisor condition, proved in this file as the theorem
    79	`Scheme.Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial` (blueprint
    80	`lem:relative_divisor_base_change`): the kernel of the pulled-back quotient
    81	is the pullback of the kernel — because `0 → I → O → O_D → 0` stays exact
    82	after base change, `Tor_1` against the `T`-flat `O_D` vanishing (Kleiman §3,
    83	functoriality note after `df:div`: "Since `D` is `T`-flat, `p_{X_T}^* I`
    84	equals the ideal of `D_{T'}`") — and pullback preserves invertibility
    85	(`IsLocallyTrivial.pullback`, Stacks 01HH).  The theorem carries a
    86	quasi-coherence hypothesis on the source of the quotient (removable once
    87	extension-closure of quasi-coherence, Stacks 01LA, is available; see the
    88	declaration docstring), discharged here by `pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom` +
    89	`Modules.unit_isQuasicoherent` since the source is the pulled-back unit.
    90	The supporting lemmas — the Stacks 00HL algebra heart
    91	`Module.Flat.rTensor_injective_of_exact`, the comparison map
    92	`Modules.pullbackKernelComparison`, and the chart-shrinking lemmas — live in
    93	`Picard/FlatKernelBase.lean`; the derivation of the pinned statement from
    94	the isomorphism form of the comparison is
    95	`Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial_of_isIso_kernelComparison` (§0).
    96	
    97	The functor laws are verbatim the pseudofunctor-coherence argument of
    98	`Scheme.QuotFunctor` (`Modules.pullback_id_app_coherence`,
    99	`Modules.pullback_comp_app_coherence_inv`), which was stated in
   100	`QuotFunctorDef.lean` for arbitrary modules and so applies to the unit.

     9	/-!
    10	# The pullback–tensor comparison with one trivialised factor
    11	
    12	This file records the **one-sided reduction** of the pullback–tensor comparison
    13	`Scheme.Modules.pullbackTensorMap f P Q : f^*(P ⊗ Q) ⟶ f^*P ⊗ f^*Q`
    14	(`Picard/TensorObjSubstrate.lean`): invertibility for a *locally trivial* second
    15	factor `Q` and an **arbitrary** first factor `P` reduces to the single residual
    16	statement `pullbackTensorMap f P 𝒪_X` — the "twist an arbitrary sheaf by the
    17	structure sheaf" case.
    18	
    19	## Why this shape, and what it is for
    20	
    21	The campaign milestone D2' (`AJC.picrep.divgrassmannian`) needs the comparison at
    22	`P ⊗ L^{⊗m}` where `P` is a *quotient sheaf of a divisor family* — not locally
    23	free, not trivialisable — and `L^{⊗m}` is a line bundle. The landed
    24	`Modules.pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial`
    25	(`Picard/TensorObjSubstrate/PullbackTensorIso.lean:153`) requires **both**
    26	factors locally trivial, so it does not apply; the general statement
    27	`Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso` (`Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean:458`) is a
    28	`sorry`. Between those two lies exactly the shape a twist needs, and this file
    29	measures how much of it is free.
    30	
    31	## What is proved here, and what is not
    32	
    33	* `pullbackTensorMap_isIso_of_right_iso_unit` — **PROVED, sorry-free**: if the
    34	  second factor is *isomorphic to* the structure sheaf, invertibility transfers
    35	  from the structure-sheaf case. The first factor is arbitrary. This is the step
    36	  that removes the second local-triviality hypothesis of
    37	  `pullbackTensorMap_isIso_of_base_unit`, whose proof this one mirrors with
    38	  `𝟙 P` in place of a trivialisation of `P`; naturality
    39	  (`pullbackTensorMap_natural`) is unconditional, which is what makes the
    40	  substitution legitimate.
    41	
    42	* `PullbackTensorRightUnit` — the **residual obligation**, carried as a
    43	  `Prop`-class with **no instance**, exactly the house pattern for a statement
    44	  that is true but unproved (contrast `HasSmoothProperQuotient`, and see
    45	  protection `I-0074` caveat 2 on why a global instance would be the wrong move).
    46	  Its field mentions both `f` and `P`: it asserts invertibility of
    47	  `pullbackTensorMap f P 𝒪_X`, so there is no way to satisfy it without saying
    48	  something about the morphism and the sheaf it is about.
    49	
    50	* `pullbackTensorMap_isIso_of_right_locallyTrivial` — the assembly: from the
    51	  residual class plus local triviality of `Q` alone, invertibility at `P ⊗ Q`
    52	  for arbitrary `P`. **This is an implication, not a discharge**: the class it
    53	  binds has no producer in the project, and this file does not claim one.
    54	
    55	## The honest accounting
    56	
    57	**D2''s twist comparison needs no gate at all** — `pullbackTensorIsoOfTwist`
    58	below builds `f^*(P ⊗ L) ≅ f^*P ⊗ f^*L` for an arbitrary `P` and an `L ≅ 𝒪_X`,
    59	sorry-free and unconditionally.
    60	
    61	An earlier version of this file gated that behind the class
    62	`PullbackTensorRightUnit` and asserted that "no unitor-compatibility lemma for
    63	`pullbackTensorMap` exists in the project or in Mathlib `v4.31`". **That absence
    64	claim was false**, and it is corrected here rather than quietly dropped: the
    65	square exists as `Modules.pullbackTensorMap_left_unitality`
    66	(`Picard/TensorObjInverse.lean:2377`), proved in a file with no `sorry` from the
    67	free presheaf coherence `Functor.OplaxMonoidal.left_unitality_hom`. It was
    68	declared `private`, which is why a search for it failed; it is now exported (the
    69	only edit this file's landing makes outside itself). The lesson, since the shape
    70	recurs: a symmetric operator has **two** unitor squares, and the search was run
    71	on the side the consumer happened to stand on.
    72	
    73	So the accounting is:
    74	
    75	* **left-hand unit case, arbitrary second factor** — unconditional
    76	  (`pullbackTensorMap_isIso_of_left_unit`), from that square;
    77	* **right-hand unit case, arbitrary first factor** — unconditional *as an
    78	  `Iso`* (`pullbackTensorIsoOfTwist`), by transporting the left case across
    79	  `tensorObj_braiding`, which is itself unconditional;
    80	* the class `PullbackTensorRightUnit` survives only for the residual it really
    81	  is: invertibility of the *specific map* `pullbackTensorMap f P 𝒪_X` **on the
    82	  nose**. Braiding transports the object and the isomorphism, not that map, so
    83	  the on-the-nose statement still wants a right-handed twin of
    84	  `pullbackTensorMap_left_unitality`. Mathlib carries
    85	  `Functor.OplaxMonoidal.right_unitality_hom`, the same free source the left one
